item.title: Eastern North Pacific Tropical Weather Outlook
item.description:
992
ABPZ20 KNHC 052310
TWOEP

Tropical Weather Outlook
NWS National Hurricane Center Miami FL
500 PM PDT Sat Sep 5 2026

For the eastern and central North Pacific east of 180 longitude:

Active Systems:
The National Hurricane Center is issuing advisories on Hurricane
Lowell, located about 600 miles south-southwest of the Hawaiian
Islands, on recently downgraded Tropical Storm Karina, located about
750 miles east-northeast of the Hawaiian Islands, and on Hurricane
Marie, located several hundred miles west of the southern tip of the
Baja California Peninsula.

Offshore of Southwestern Mexico:
A trough of low pressure located several hundred miles south of the
coast of southwestern Mexico is producing disorganized showers and
thunderstorms. Gradual development of this system is possible, and a
tropical depression could form during the middle or latter portions
of next week while the system moves generally west-northwestward at
10 to 15 mph.
* Formation chance through 48 hours...low...near 0 percent.
* Formation chance through 7 days...medium...60 percent.

$$
Forecaster Cangialosi

item.title: Hurricane Marie Public Advisory Number 20
item.description:
Issued at 800 PM PDT Sat Sep 05 2026 
000
WTPZ33 KNHC 060232
TCPEP3
 
BULLETIN
Hurricane Marie Advisory Number  20
NWS National Hurricane Center Miami FL       EP132026
800 PM PDT Sat Sep 05 2026
 
...MARIE FORECAST TO BEGIN WEAKENING ON SUNDAY...
 
 
SUMMARY OF 800 PM PDT...0300 UTC...INFORMATION
----------------------------------------------
LOCATION...22.6N 121.3W
ABOUT 725 MI...1170 KM W OF THE SOUTHERN TIP OF BAJA CALIFORNIA
MAXIMUM SUSTAINED WINDS...90 MPH...150 KM/H
PRESENT MOVEMENT...NW OR 315 DEGREES AT 6 MPH...9 KM/H
MINIMUM CENTRAL PRESSURE...970 MB...28.65 INCHES
 
 
WATCHES AND WARNINGS
--------------------
There are no coastal watches or warnings in effect.
 
 
DISCUSSION AND OUTLOOK
----------------------
At 800 PM PDT (0300 UTC), the center of Hurricane Marie was located 
near latitude 22.6 North, longitude 121.3 West. Marie is moving 
toward the northwest near 6 mph (9 km/h) and this motion is expected 
to continue through Sunday. A turn toward the west-northwest is 
forecast early next week. Marie is then expected to resume a 
northwestward heading at a faster forward speed by Tuesday.
 
Maximum sustained winds are near 90 mph (150 km/h) with higher 
gusts. Steady weakening is expected for the next several days, and 
Marie is forecast to become a post-tropical remnant low on 
Wednesday. 
 
Hurricane-force winds extend outward up to 50 miles (85 km) from the
center and tropical-storm-force winds extend outward up to 185 miles
(295 km).
 
The estimated minimum central pressure is 970 mb (28.65 inches).
 
 
HAZARDS AFFECTING LAND
----------------------
SURF: Swells generated by Marie will continue to affect portions of
the coast of southwest Mexico, the Baja California Peninsula, and
Southern California for the next few days. These swells are likely
to cause life-threatening surf and rip current conditions. Please
consult products from your local weather office. A depiction of rip
current risk for the United States can be found at:
hurricanes.gov/graphics_ep3.shtml?ripCurrents
 
 
NEXT ADVISORY
-------------
Next complete advisory at 200 AM PDT.
 
$$
Forecaster Adams

item.title: Hurricane Marie Forecast Discussion Number 19
item.description:
Issued at 200 PM PDT Sat Sep 05 2026 
000
WTPZ43 KNHC 052040
TCDEP3
 
Hurricane Marie Discussion Number  19
NWS National Hurricane Center Miami FL       EP132026
200 PM PDT Sat Sep 05 2026
 
Marie continues to exhibit a large ragged eye, around 60 n mi in
diameter. Satellite estimates of the hurricane's intensity are very
similar to what they were 6 hours ago, and therefore the initial
intensity remains 80 kt for this advisory. The heading of
the hurricane has been similarly steady, albeit at a slightly 
slower forward speed, with a motion estimate of 305/6 kt.

Marie is moving along the western periphery of a ridge centered over 
the southern United States and will likely continue on a generally 
northwestward heading for most of the weekend. A short-term bend 
toward the west-northwest is still expected early next week as the 
cyclone weakens but it will ultimately accelerate northwestward as a 
mid- to upper-level trough digs quickly southward to the west of 
Marie by late Tuesday.

A drier environment and cooler SSTs are still expected to cause 
Marie to slowly weaken during the next couple of days. The rate of 
weakening could increase after that as the environment gets more 
hostile and the aforementioned trough causes an increase in 
southerly wind shear across the cyclone. Marie is still expected to 
become a post-tropical remnant low near the 96 h mark, and could 
dissipate in about 5 days, though the forecast conservatively shows 
a point at that time for now. The NHC track and intensity forecasts 
are very close to the HCCA and GDM consensus aids.
